title.narrative: 223922_Mexico - Anticipation of spike in cross border migration

description.narrative:
This is an anticipatory action project aiming to pre-position supplies for meeting food security needs, non-food item needs, shelter, psychosocial support, and livelihoods needs. The needs are predicted to arise from the recently announced changes to immigration policies by the new USA Government. The abrupt cancellation of the CBP One application, the reinstatement of the "Remain in Mexico" program, and the beginning of mass deportation campaigns have altered migration flows and strained local resources in cities such as Tijuana, Tapachula, and Sonora. Thousands of migrants have been left stranded or forced to return to precarious situations, increasing pressure on shelters, public services and the labor market. In Tijuana, uncertainty has led many to reconsider their immigration plans, while in Tapachula, the stagnation in regularization processes has turned the city into a bottleneck. In Sonora, authorities are trying to expand the capacity of shelters in the face of an imminent increase in deportees, although the available resources are insufficient to address the emerging crisis.
Based on previous experiences the uncertainy of this kind of migration policy changes causes people to mobilize and concentrate which leads to a saturatio of the shelters and public services in crossborder cities. Additionally, the announced mass deportations can also increase the concentration on border cities as they are usually sent to a same point of entry and remain in those cities for a few days before being dispersed. As of right now, thousands (270,000) of people who had a CBP One appointment are stranded today in Mexico without options and in search of alternative plans, but as long as the uncertainty continues, it is not likely that they will leave but will rather stay in border cities and saturate services. We are anticipating a severe situation, as Mexico is a country of transit, destination and origin and this kind of changes motivate movement.
